properties.trigger: any competition, team, match, player or stat in cricket: Tests, ODIs, T20Is, franchise T20 and hundred-ball leagues, club and league cricket, fantasy cricket
properties.scope: competition, season, team, person, event, stat_line

data.short_description: Cricket. Vocabulary for the Sports World: positions and bowling styles, stages and rounds, the periods array (one element per innings) and result rules (draws, ties, no results, DLS, super overs, margins, the toss), batting, bowling and fielding stat keys with the exact formulas for average, strike rate and economy, standings with net run rate and championship percentage, squads versus the XI, replacements, officials. Covers international, franchise and club cricket.

lore.title: Overview
lore.content:
Cricket. A match is a match (fixture or game in club talk; Test, ODI, T20I, T20 or hundred-ball match by format). Two sides of eleven. The match is divided into innings: one per side in limited-overs cricket (ODI, List A, T20, T100, club 40- or 45-over games), two per side in Tests, first-class and two-day club cricket. An innings is divided into overs of six legal balls (five-ball sets in hundred-ball cricket, whose innings is 100 balls). A side's innings ends when ten wickets fall (all out), when its allotted balls run out, when the captain declares, when the target is reached, or when the match ends.

What the single score number is: home_score and away_score are each side's total runs across its innings, excluding super overs. They are display figures only. Never read result from them: a side can lose with more runs (declaration, DLS), and a drawn Test is a draw whatever the totals. result comes from the owner's statement of the result; margin_type and margin carry how big it was; score_display carries the full line as a scorer writes it (Riverside 287/6 (50) v Castleton 251 (48.3); Castleton 301 & 196 v Riverside 287 & 312/4d). The periods array on the event, one element per innings, is the structured truth behind all of that (see the chunk Innings and results).

Draws, ties, no results: all three exist and are distinct. draw: a match that ran out of time with the fourth innings unfinished (Tests, first-class, timed club cricket). tie: both sides all out or out of balls on the same total; when a super over follows, the match result is the super over's winner with decided_by super_over, and the tie is visible in periods. no_result: abandoned or rained off without reaching the minimum overs for a result; it is neither win nor loss and does not break a streak. Limited-overs matches cannot be drawn.

Match formats (match_format on the competition, overridden per event when a competition mixes them): test (five days, two innings a side, unlimited overs), first_class (three or four days, two innings), odi and list_a (50 overs a side), limited_overs_40 and limited_overs_45 (club one-day formats; set balls_allotted accordingly), t20 (20 overs), t100 (hundred-ball cricket, 100 balls a side), two_day (club two-innings matches, often over two Saturdays), timed (club declaration cricket with a time limit, a draw possible), other.

Default competition shape: a bilateral series between two national sides (a five-Test series with a trophy, a three-match ODI series) is a competition with format series and one season per edition, each Test or ODI a match event with round 1st Test, 2nd ODI. A franchise or club league is format league (table only) or league_playoffs (most franchise T20 and hundred-ball leagues). A world tournament is group_knockout. Default scoring_system: 2-1-0 for limited overs (2 win, 1 tie or no result, 0 loss) and for bilateral series; 12-6-4-0_pct for a multi-year Test championship league (12 win, 6 tie, 4 draw, table by percentage of points available); custom for club leagues with bonus points, stated in a House rules chunk on the competition.

A series or tour is a season of a competition with format series, not a parent event, as rule/recording_a_match says: see Series and tours. Multi-day matches carry date_* of day one and end_date of the last day; a day/night match is tagged day-night. Every entity in this sport carries the tag cricket.

lore.title: Positions
lore.content:
Position codes on PLAYS_FOR (position) and on PLAYED_IN (position on the day). One primary; others in secondary_positions.
batter: picked mainly to bat. Opening batters may carry the tag opener.
bowler: picked mainly to bowl. Style is a tag on the person (see below), not a position.
all_rounder: picked for both bat and ball.
wicketkeeper: keeps wicket. A keeper who is also a front-line batter is still wicketkeeper here; say so in the description.
Captaincy is role captain or vice_captain on PLAYS_FOR (standing) and captain true on PLAYED_IN (on the day), never a position.

Handedness on the person uses the composite form, mirroring the base's example: bats_right_bowls_right, bats_right_bowls_left, bats_left_bowls_right, bats_left_bowls_left, bats_right, bats_left (non-bowlers). Bowling style is one controlled tag on the person, lowercase with hyphens: right-arm-fast, right-arm-fast-medium, right-arm-medium, right-arm-off-spin, right-arm-leg-spin, left-arm-fast, left-arm-fast-medium, left-arm-medium, left-arm-orthodox, left-arm-wrist-spin. Add no other style tags; a mystery spinner is whichever of these the owner says.

Fantasy slots (slot on a fantasy roster edge), for the common daily-fantasy format: WK, BAT, AR, BOWL, C (captain, 2x), VC (vice-captain, 1.5x), BN. Lineup counts are a house rule on the fantasy competition.

lore.title: Stages and rounds
lore.content:
stage values on match events:
regular_season: the league phase of a franchise or club league (a franchise T20 league's league stage, Saturday league rounds).
group_stage: the group phase of a world tournament or qualifier.
super_stage: a second group phase (a super-eight or super-six round).
playoff: a franchise-league playoff round that is not a semi or final; round says which: Qualifier 1, Eliminator, Qualifier 2, Knockout, Challenger.
quarterfinal, semifinal, final: as named.
series: any match in a bilateral series or tour (Test, ODI, T20I, first-class or List A tour match between the two sides).
warm_up: official warm-up or practice match before a tournament; counts for nothing.
tour_match: a touring side against a non-international opponent (a county, a President's XI).
friendly: club friendlies and midweek games that do not count toward a league.
cup: a club knockout cup round when the cup is tracked inside the league season; round holds the round name.

round, written as people say it: 1st Test, 2nd ODI, 3rd T20I, Match 23 (franchise leagues number their matches), Round 7 or Week 12 (club leagues), Qualifier 1, Eliminator, Group B Match 4, Semi-final 2, Day 1 is never a round (days are one match).

decided_by values:
regulation: a normal result, including a draw or a tie with no super over.
dls: the standard rain-rule method's revised target applied (also use for its older two-letter predecessor).
vjd: the alternative rain-rule method used in some domestic cricket.
super_over: tie settled by one or more super overs.
bowl_out: historic tie-break by bowling at unguarded stumps.
boundary_count: historic tie-break on boundaries scored (used once in a famous tournament final).
walkover: the opponent did not turn up or withdrew; status forfeited.
awarded: result awarded by the match referee or league (refusal to play, ineligible player); status forfeited, the ruling in lore.

margin_type values (with margin as the number): runs (36), wickets (5), innings_and_runs (margin holds the runs part: an innings and 46 runs is innings_and_runs 46), super_over (margin is the super-over runs difference), none for draws, ties and no results (leave both blank). Balls remaining in a chase is derived from the last innings (balls_allotted minus balls), not stored.

toss: toss_won_by holds the slug of the side that won the toss, toss_decision is bat or bowl (or unknown). Who batted first is read from periods[0].batting_team, never stored a second time.

lore.title: Stat keys
lore.content:
All counting stats are stored as integers. Balls are always stored as balls, never overs: 4.3 overs is 27 balls. Overs are displayed as floor(balls / 6) and balls mod 6 (27 balls shows as 4.3; hundred-ball cricket shows balls). Nothing in stats is text; dismissal text and bowling figures as written go in lore (see rule/cricket_scorecard_entry).

Player match line (scope match, RECORDED_IN the match). A player who did not bat has the batting keys null and innings_batted 0; same for bowling. Every line carries completeness: full when the whole card was entered, partial when some keys are null because nobody kept them, unknown for typed-in totals of unknown coverage; sums skip nulls and a season line built from any partial line is partial.

Batting
innings_batted: innings in which the player batted (faced a ball or was dismissed without facing one). 0, 1 or 2 in a match.
not_outs: innings batted that ended not out, including retired_not_out.
runs: runs scored off the bat (excluding extras).
balls_faced: legal balls faced (wides not counted; no-balls counted).
fours: boundary fours hit.
sixes: sixes hit.
dots_faced: dot balls faced, when the owner tracks them.
ducks: dismissals for 0.
fifties: innings of 50 to 99.
hundreds: innings of 100 or more (a 150 or 200 is also one hundred; the owner can add double_hundreds as an extended key).
highest_score: best single innings, season and career lines only; highest_score_not_out 1 when that innings was not out.
Dismissal counts, 0 or 1 in a match line and totals in season lines; exactly one of them is 1 per completed innings unless not out:
out_bowled, out_caught, out_lbw, out_run_out, out_stumped, out_hit_wicket, out_other (handled the ball/obstructing, hit the ball twice, timed out), out_retired (retired out, counts as a dismissal), retired_not_out (retired and did not resume; counts as not out, so it is also counted in not_outs). No reason for a retirement is ever recorded.

Bowling
innings_bowled: innings in which the player bowled at least one ball.
balls_bowled: legal balls bowled (wides and no-balls are not legal balls and are not counted here).
maidens: overs with no runs conceded off the bat or as wides or no-balls.
runs_conceded: runs charged to the bowler (bat runs plus wides plus no-balls; byes and leg byes are not charged).
wickets: wickets credited to the bowler (not run outs).
wides: wides bowled (count of balls, not runs).
no_balls: no-balls bowled (count of balls).
dots_bowled: dot balls bowled, when tracked.
four_wicket_hauls: innings of exactly 4 wickets (limited overs).
five_wicket_hauls: innings of 5 or more wickets.
ten_wicket_matches: matches of 10 or more wickets (two-innings matches).
best_bowling_wickets and best_bowling_runs: best innings figures (most wickets, then fewest runs), season and career lines only.

Fielding and wicketkeeping
catches: catches taken as a fielder (not as keeper).
wk_catches: catches taken while keeping.
stumpings: stumpings.
run_outs: run outs the player was credited with (direct hit or the thrower in an assisted run out; the owner may add run_outs_direct and run_outs_assisted as extended keys).
byes_conceded: byes while keeping, when tracked.
drops: dropped catches, when the owner tracks them (club sides often do).

General
matches: matches played (season and career lines; mirrors games_played and is kept for leaders queries).
player_of_match: Player of the Match awards. Also recorded as a WON edge to the event; the key is a count for leaders.
fantasy_points: fantasy points for a fantasy matchup line (see Fantasy).

Derived rate stats (never stored on match lines; stored on season or career lines only when the owner types a published figure in, source official or owner, and then with the components left as given):
batting_average = runs / (innings_batted - not_outs). The denominator is dismissals. When dismissals is 0 the average is undefined: show a dash and quote the runs (e.g. 101* in 2 innings), never divide by zero and never show the runs as the average.
strike_rate = runs * 100 / balls_faced (runs per hundred balls).
boundary_percentage = (fours * 4 + sixes * 6) * 100 / runs, when asked.
bowling_average = runs_conceded / wickets; undefined when wickets is 0 (show a dash).
economy = runs_conceded * 6 / balls_bowled (runs per six-ball over). For a t100 competition say so and offer runs per 5-ball set = runs_conceded * 5 / balls_bowled as well.
bowling_strike_rate = balls_bowled / wickets; undefined when wickets is 0.
dot_ball_percentage = dots_bowled * 100 / balls_bowled, when dots are tracked.
A season or career line sums the match lines (rule/stats): innings_batted, not_outs and runs sum, so the average is recomputed from the sums, never averaged across matches.

Two-innings matches: the match line holds both innings summed (innings_batted 2). When the owner wants the card per innings, add a stat_line with scope segment and segment 1 or 2, RECORDED_IN the match. Season lines sum match lines only, never the segment lines.

Team match line (scope match, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the match), optional, for totals the periods array does not carry:
extras: total extras conceded by this side's bowlers and fielders.
byes, leg_byes, wides_conceded, no_balls_conceded, penalty_runs: the breakdown of extras.
boundaries_hit: fours plus sixes as a side, when asked for.
Team season line keys are in Standings.

lore.title: Standings
lore.content:
Team season line (scope season, subject_kind team, RECORDED_IN the season, STAT_OF the team, source derived unless the owner types the table in). Keys:
played: matches with a result, a tie, a draw or a no result (abandoned matches that count as no result are played; matches declared void or cancelled before the toss are not).
won, lost, tied, drawn, no_results: as named.
points: competition points under the scoring system (win 2, tie 1, no result 1, loss 0 by default; Test championship 12/6/4/0; club house rules).
bonus_points, penalty_points: added to and subtracted from points when the competition uses them (batting and bowling bonus points, slow over-rate deductions, as the league states them in lore on the event).
points_available: the maximum points the team could have taken from its matches so far (a Test championship league: 12 per match). Required for a pct table.
runs_scored: runs scored by the team in all innings of matches that count toward NRR.
balls_faced_total: balls the team is charged with facing, after the all-out rule below.
runs_conceded: runs the team conceded in those matches.
balls_bowled_total: balls the team is charged with bowling, after the all-out rule.
net_run_rate: stored on the season line (it is the standard column), source derived, and rebuilt from the four keys above whenever the line is rebuilt. Never type it in from a published table without setting source official.
pct: percentage of points, stored only on season lines of competitions with scoring_system 12-6-4-0_pct, derived.

Formulas:
net_run_rate = (runs_scored / (balls_faced_total / 6)) - (runs_conceded / (balls_bowled_total / 6)), to two decimals, sign shown (+0.412, -1.105).
All-out rule: when a side is bowled out, its balls for NRR are its full allotted balls (balls_allotted on that innings, which is the revised quota in a DLS-shortened match), not the balls it actually faced. A side that reaches its target with balls to spare is charged only the balls it faced.
DLS rule: in a match decided by dls, the side batting first is charged target - 1 runs in the revised allotted balls (the par score), not its actual total; the chasing side is charged its actual runs and balls (or its revised quota if all out).
Exclusions: no_result and abandoned matches contribute nothing to NRR; super overs contribute nothing; tied matches contribute their actual figures; forfeited matches contribute nothing unless the competition's house rules say otherwise.
pct = (points - penalty_points) * 100 / points_available, to two decimals.

Columns to show:
Limited overs (odi, list_a, t20, t100, club one-day): P W L T NR Pts NRR.
Two-innings league (Test championship, first-class, two_day club): P W L D T (Pts) Pct, with NRR omitted unless the league uses it.
Club leagues with bonus points: P W L T NR Bonus Pen Pts, NRR last.

Tiebreakers, applied in this order unless the competition's House rules chunk says otherwise:
Limited overs (default, international tournaments and most franchise leagues): 1. points; 2. most wins; 3. net_run_rate; 4. head-to-head points between the tied sides; 5. head-to-head NRR; 6. the owner decides (the regulations usually say seeding or a draw of lots), say so.
Test championship league: 1. pct; 2. most series won; 3. net_run_rate across the cycle; 4. wickets taken per run conceded across the cycle, which this world does not compute: say so.
Group-then-knockout world tournaments: as limited overs, within each group (group on COMPETES_IN).
Name the tiebreaker that split any two sides. A table with a stale season line (as_of older than the latest completed match) is rebuilt from the periods arrays and COMPETED_IN results first, per rule/seasons_and_standings. Dot-path filters reach inside periods: search_entities with entity_type event and a filter on properties.periods.0.batting_team eq <team> returns every match that side batted first in, so "who batted first" and the NRR rebuild are one filter per side, not a scan of the season.

lore.title: Roster rules
lore.content:
Squad versus XI: a squad (15 to 18 internationally, as many as turn up at club level) is the open PLAYS_FOR edges on the team; the playing XI for a match is the PLAYED_IN edges with started true. Players named in a squad but left out carry PLAYED_IN played false (international and franchise squads, and club "12th man" or scorer-who-is-also-a-player cases). Eleven started per side, no more; if the owner names twelve, ask who was twelfth.

Batting order: lineup_order 1 to 11 on PLAYED_IN is the order they batted (or were listed to bat); did-not-bat players keep their listed order and have innings_batted 0 on their line. Captain on the day: captain true. Keeper on the day: position wicketkeeper on PLAYED_IN when it differs from the roster position.

Substitutes and replacements: cricket has no rolling substitutions. Three kinds of replacement exist and are all recorded the same way: the outgoing player's PLAYED_IN gets replaced_by with the incoming player's slug; the incoming player gets PLAYED_IN started false, played true, entered_at (over or innings: 7th over, 2nd innings). The kinds: an impact player (some franchise T20 leagues: a tactical replacement, both players' stats count), a like-for-like replacement approved by the match referee, and a substitute fielder (who can field but not bat or bowl; give them played true, started false and a lore note). The reason for a like-for-like replacement is a health matter and is never recorded; if the owner gives it, write who replaced whom and say in one line that this world keeps no health details. The same goes for a batter who retires: the card says retired, the stats say retired_not_out or out_retired, nothing more.

Availability (Saturday XI): availability on PLAYS_FOR is available, unavailable, doubtful, suspended or unknown. "Can't make it", "away that weekend", "working" are all unavailable with no reason stored. A ban from the league (slow over rate, conduct) is suspended with the league's stated terms in lore on the person. See rule/cricket_saturday_xi for the weekly selection workflow.

Eligibility checks before logging a lineup, when the competition states them in House rules: overseas-player limits (franchise leagues typically allow two to four, first-class domestic leagues one or two); club league limits on registered players and on players who have played a higher division that season; youth age bands (Under-13, Under-15, Under-19) which make every player on the side a minor: is_minor true, first name and last initial, no birth date, no profile links (league and club scoring websites are not sources for private people even when public), no web lookups. A club player's registration number is external_id only when the owner asks for it to be kept.

Bowling limits worth checking when the owner logs figures: in a 50-over match no bowler bowls more than 10 overs (60 balls), in a T20 no more than 4 (24 balls), in hundred-ball cricket no more than 20 balls; club leagues set their own. If a logged figure exceeds the limit, ask before saving.

Roles and staff: head_coach, assistant_coach with unit batting, bowling or fielding; manager for the team manager; captain_organiser for the club captain who also picks the side and collects match fees (PLAYS_FOR and STAFF_OF both); treasurer, scout, analyst as the base lists. Selectors are STAFF_OF with role other and title Selector. A club's 1st XI, 2nd XI and Sunday XI are separate teams PART_OF the club's senior side.

lore.title: Officials
lore.content:
OFFICIATED role values:
on_field_umpire: one of the two standing umpires (bowler's end and striker's end rotate; do not distinguish).
third_umpire: the TV umpire (also called the DRS umpire).
fourth_umpire: the reserve umpire at an international match.
match_referee: the match referee appointed by the governing body.
scorer: official scorer; club sides often name their own, one per side, so two scorer edges are normal.
umpire: a club or league umpire when the owner does not distinguish ends or there is only one; a player standing at square leg for their own side is not an official and gets no edge.
reserve_umpire: as named, domestic cricket.
Record officials only when the owner names them, per rule/recording_a_match.

lore.title: Extended keys
lore.content: (none yet) Keys the owner adds later go here, one per line as key: meaning, dated YYYY-MM-DD, before they are used in any stat_line.

lore.title: Innings and results
lore.content:
The periods array on the match event is the structured record of the match. One element per innings in the order played, including super overs. Keys per element (every element carries number; the rest are this pack's keys):
number: 1, 2, 3, 4 in order played; super overs continue the count.
batting_team: slug of the side batting.
runs: runs scored in the innings (including extras).
wickets: wickets lost (10 when all out; also 10 when a side is all out with a batter absent or retired; 9 or fewer with declared true or balls exhausted).
balls: legal balls faced (48.3 overs is 291).
balls_allotted: the innings' quota in balls when the format has one: 300 for an ODI, 240 for a T20, 100 for hundred-ball cricket, 240 or 270 for 40- or 45-over club cricket; the revised quota after a DLS reduction; null for Tests, first-class, two_day and timed matches.
all_out: true when ten wickets fell (or the side was all out with fewer because of absences).
declared: true when the captain declared (two-innings matches only).
follow_on: true on the innings a side bats after being made to follow on (it is that side's second innings and the match's third).
forfeited: true when a side forfeited the innings (two-innings cricket; the innings has runs 0, wickets 0, balls 0).
target: the runs the batting side needed to win, on the final (or any chasing) innings; the DLS-revised target when one applied.
kind: regular or super_over.

From it the AI derives, and never stores a second time: who batted first (periods[0].batting_team), home_score and away_score (the sum of each side's regular innings runs; set them on the event as the headline figures), the margin check (runs: the winner's total minus the loser's; wickets: 10 minus the chasing side's wickets lost; innings_and_runs: when the winner needed only one innings and the loser's two innings together fell short by margin runs), balls remaining in a chase (balls_allotted minus balls), the overs display, and the NRR inputs under the all-out and DLS rules in Standings.

Results, from the owner's statement, never from the arithmetic:
A side reaches its target: result for that side (home_win or away_win), margin_type wickets, margin 10 minus wickets lost, decided_by regulation (or dls when the target was revised).
The side batting last falls short and is all out or out of balls: margin_type runs, margin the difference. Two-innings cricket where the side batting last needed to bat only once fewer: margin_type innings_and_runs.
Scores level and no super over: result tie, both COMPETED_IN result tie. With a super over: periods elements kind super_over for each side (and more if the super over was itself tied and repeated), result the winner, decided_by super_over, margin_type super_over, margin the super-over difference.
Time runs out with the fourth innings unfinished (or the third, or the second in a timed club match): result draw, both COMPETED_IN result draw, margin blank.
Weather or light ends it before the minimum overs for a result (internationally 20 overs per side in ODIs, 5 in T20s; club leagues vary): status abandoned, result no_result, decided_by blank, periods holding what was played, score_display with the position at the stoppage.
A side does not turn up or refuses to play: status forfeited, decided_by walkover or awarded, periods empty, the ruling in lore.

score_display is written as a scorer would: for one-innings matches "Riverside 287/6 (50) v Castleton 251 (48.3)", for two-innings "Castleton 301 & 196 v Riverside 287 & 312/4d", with "(f/o)" after a follow-on innings and "(target 187 off 32 ov, DLS)" when revised. A super over is appended as "(SO 12-9)".

Order of writing when a result comes in (rule/cricket_scorecard_entry has the full workflow): event status and dates; periods; home_score, away_score, score_display; result, decided_by, margin_type, margin; toss_won_by, toss_decision; COMPETED_IN result on both edges; then player and team stat_lines; then the team season lines in the same breath.

lore.title: Series and tours
lore.content:
A bilateral series or a tour is a season of a competition with format series, not a parent event; rule/recording_a_match states this for any series that is the whole competition between two sides, and this pack confirms it. Rationale: the base defines a competition as the standing thing that runs year after year with a season per edition; a Test series between two sides is exactly that (the oldest rivalry series has run since the 1880s and has a trophy; several other pairings have named trophies), and even an unnamed series ("Home v Away ODIs") recurs every few years between the same pair in the same format. Modelling each as a season gives the series score for free: the team season lines hold won, lost, drawn, tied, no_results; COMPETES_IN final_rank 1 and outcome champion mark the series winner; a WON edge from the winning team to the season with title the trophy's name (or "Series" when there is none) says who holds it; a retained trophy after a drawn series is WON with title and detail "retained (series drawn 2-2)". get_timeline filtered on the season tag gives the series in order.

How to set one up: competition named for the trophy when it has one (format series, level international, match_format test, governing_body the two boards), otherwise "<Home> v <Away> <Format> series" (home side first; the return series in the other country is a different competition because the host changes and the pairing is written the other way). Season label the edition as people say it: "2027-28" for a southern-hemisphere winter series, "2026" for a northern summer tour. rounds_total the number of matches in the series; round on each match "1st Test", "2nd Test"; stage series. Tag the season with its series tag (trophy-series-2027-28) and every match with it. A tour with Tests, ODIs and T20Is is three competitions and three seasons sharing a tour tag (away-tour-2026-27); say so when the owner asks "how did the tour go".

A best-of-N playoff series inside a franchise season does not exist in cricket; the base's parent-event pattern for series is not used by this pack. A tournament inside a season (a club's midweek T20 cup run inside the league season) is a parent event with stage cup, per the base.

Series standings: there is no NRR in a bilateral series; the table is simply the series score. When a series also counts toward a wider league (a Test championship cycle, an ODI league), the match is credited to that league's season as well: one match event, PART_OF the series season, with a second tag for the league cycle, and the league's season lines count it. Never create the match twice.

lore.title: Recreational
lore.content:
What club and league cricket changes. Formats: 40-, 45- or 50-over Saturday leagues, timed or two-day declaration cricket (a draw is possible and common), midweek T20 and 100-ball evening leagues, Sunday friendlies that count for nothing (stage friendly). Set match_format on the competition and balls_allotted from it; club leagues often have a bowler limit of a fifth of the overs and a fielding-restriction rule that does not matter to this record.
Points: most leagues use a points table with bonus points (batting bonus by runs scored, bowling bonus by wickets taken) and penalties (slow over rate, unregistered player); the table is points then NRR or then wins, as the House rules chunk on the competition says. Winning draws and losing draws exist in timed cricket: both are result draw, with the league's points in bonus_points, and the owner's description in lore.
Stat keeping is sporadic: a result and the owner's own line is a complete entry; tag the event scorecard-pending and ask for the card later. Averages for the club dinner need a qualification (minimum innings or overs); state it when presenting.
Rolling player pools: a club with a 1st XI, 2nd XI and Sunday side moves players between them weekly; each XI is a team PART_OF the club, each player has one open PLAYS_FOR edge to the club side they mainly play for, and a match for another XI is a PLAYED_IN with for_team that XI, no roster change. Ringers: PLAYS_FOR with arrangement substitute, started and ended on the match date.
Juniors playing senior cricket and youth leagues: every under-18 is a minor; see Roster rules. Teas, fees, umpiring rota and who drives are lore, never properties. The weekly rhythm is rule/cricket_saturday_xi.

lore.title: Professional
lore.content:
What the top level adds. Match formats test, odi, t20i (international T20; use match_format t20), first_class, list_a, t20 and t100 in domestic cricket. Stages: a Test championship cycle (league, two-year season, pct table), bilateral series as seasons (Series and tours), world tournaments as group_knockout with super_stage, franchise leagues as league_playoffs with the playoff round names (Qualifier 1, Eliminator, Qualifier 2, Knockout, Challenger). Day/night Tests and T20 doubleheaders: tag day-night; two matches on one day are two events with round naming each.
Squads: a touring squad of 15 to 18 is the PLAYS_FOR edges with role reserve for those outside the XI; the XI per match is PLAYED_IN started true. Overseas-player limits, salary caps, auctions and drafts: an auction is an event with event_type draft, INVOLVED_IN role drafted with detail the price as text; retention and release windows are release and signing events; a franchise's overseas slots are a House rules chunk. Central contracts are arrangement contract with fee as text.
Replacements: impact player (tactical, both players count), like-for-like replacement (approved by the match referee, no reason recorded), substitute fielder; all via replaced_by.
Officials add third_umpire, fourth_umpire and match_referee; the review system's outcomes (reviews used, overturned) are not keys unless the owner adds them under Extended keys.
Modern stats the owner may add under Extended keys when the source provides them: control percentage, false-shot percentage, expected runs, phase splits (powerplay, middle, death as split lines with split_label), bowling speeds. None are assumed; the stored vocabulary stays the scorecard's.
Rankings (a rating-system table published by the governing body) are not standings: store them as a lore chunk on the competition titled Rankings with the date, never as stat_lines.

lore.title: Fantasy
lore.content: Fantasy cricket (daily-fantasy platforms and the official tournament games) runs on rule/app_fantasy, which owns the workflows: rosters, lineups, matchups, waivers, trades and standings. A fantasy competition carries two APPLIES_TO edges, from rule/app_fantasy and from this pack. This chunk supplies only the cricket-specific material. Slots (slot on the fantasy PLAYS_FOR edge and on PLAYED_IN for a matchup): WK, BAT, AR, BOWL, C (captain, 2x), VC (vice-captain, 1.5x), BN. Default roster size: eleven active (at least one WK, three BAT, one AR, three BOWL) plus a bench the House rules chunk sets. The real keys that feed scoring are runs, balls_faced, fours, sixes, wickets, balls_bowled, runs_conceded, maidens, catches, wk_catches, stumpings, run_outs and ducks; the scored total is fantasy_points. Scoring (points per run, per wicket, per catch, bonuses for fifties and economy bands, captain multiplier) is a House rules chunk on the fantasy competition; the AI never assumes one platform's table. A daily-fantasy contest with no standing league is one season per contest only if the owner wants it kept; otherwise it is a match event with the entries' points in home_score and away_score when two-sided, and in team match lines when many-sided.

lore.title: Forfeits and abandonments
lore.content:
Forfeits: status forfeited, decided_by walkover (no-show, withdrawal) or awarded (refusal to play, ineligible player, league ruling), result for the side awarded the match, margin_type and margin blank unless the league awards a notional margin (some club leagues award a notional 5-wicket or 20-run win for NRR; if so, the House rules chunk says so and the notional figures go in score_display, never in periods). Points per the scoring system; the league's ruling verbatim in lore on the event under the title Ruling.

Abandoned: status abandoned. If no ball was bowled, periods is empty and the event stays the record that the fixture existed (it counts as played with a no result if the league says so, usually a point each; otherwise it is not played and the owner says which). If play started, periods holds what was played and score_display the position at the stoppage. result no_result unless the minimum overs were reached and a DLS result stands (then status completed, decided_by dls). A reserve day used (tournament knockouts): the same event, end_date the reserve day, a lore note.

Postponed and rearranged: status postponed, same event, new date when known, the original date in lore. Club leagues that move a washed-out fixture to a free Saturday do this constantly; never create a second event.

Conceded: a club side that concedes mid-match (short of players, light) is a completed match with result for the other side, decided_by awarded, and the position at concession in score_display.

lore.title: Glossary
lore.content: all out: ten wickets down (or fewer with absent batters). ball-by-ball: a record this world does not keep; the smallest unit is the innings and the player's match line. bye, leg bye: runs not off the bat and not charged to the bowler. declaration: a captain closing an innings early. DLS: the standard method for revising targets in interrupted matches. duck: dismissed for 0; golden duck, first ball. extras: wides, no-balls, byes, leg byes, penalty runs. follow-on: the side batting second, trailing heavily, batting again at once. innings: one side's turn to bat; also the plural. maiden: an over with no runs charged to the bowler. net run rate: the standings tiebreaker defined in Standings. not out: an innings that ended without a dismissal. over: six legal balls (five in hundred-ball cricket's sets). Player of the Match: a WON edge to the event. retired: a batter leaving the field mid-innings; this world records only whether it counts as out. super over: the one-over-a-side tiebreak after a tie. target: the runs the chasing side needs; one more than the total it must pass. the toss: toss_won_by and toss_decision on the event. wicket: a dismissal, or the pitch, or the stumps; in stats always a dismissal. XI: the playing eleven.

properties.trigger: a cricket result, scorecard, scorebook photo, innings total, batting or bowling figures, 'we won by', 'lost by', DLS, super over, declaration

data.short_description: Step-by-step order for turning a cricket result or scorecard into the periods array, the headline score, the result and margin, the players' lines and the season lines, with the reconciliation checks a scorer would do.

lore.title: Workflow
lore.content:
When the owner gives a result, a scorecard or a photo of the scorebook, work in this order and in as few calls as possible. Log what you can before asking.
1. Find the fixture: search_entities entity_type event with both team names and the date, and the season's fixtures for that round. Create it only if nothing matches (rule/recording_a_match), with match_format from the competition unless the owner says otherwise.
2. Innings: build the periods array, one element per innings in the order played, from what was said. Convert overs to balls (48.3 ov = 291). Set balls_allotted from the match_format (ODI 300, T20 240, T100 100, 40-over 240, 45-over 270; null for two-innings and timed formats) or the DLS-revised quota. Mark all_out when ten wickets fell, declared, follow_on, target on the chasing innings. If the owner gave totals but not balls for a side that was all out, balls can stay null; NRR will then use balls_allotted, which is the rule anyway. If a side batting first used its full quota and the owner gave no balls, set balls to balls_allotted.
3. Headline: home_score and away_score as the sum of each side's regular innings; score_display as a scorer writes it (Innings and results chunk); status completed.
4. Result: from the owner's words. result, decided_by, margin_type, margin. Check the margin against the innings (wickets: 10 minus wickets lost in the chase; runs: difference of totals) and, if your check disagrees with what was said, ask before saving rather than correcting silently: scorebooks have arithmetic errors and so do memories.
5. Toss: toss_won_by and toss_decision when given; otherwise leave blank, never guess from who batted first.
6. COMPETED_IN result on both edges from each side's point of view.
7. Players, only if lineups are tracked for the competition: PLAYED_IN for each named player with lineup_order, started, captain, position wicketkeeper on the day; replaced_by and the incoming player's edge for any impact player or replacement, no reason. Then one match stat_line per player with the Stat keys, completeness full when the whole card is in and partial when some keys are null: batting keys for those who batted (innings_batted 1, not_outs 1 for a not-out innings, exactly one out_* key set to 1 otherwise), bowling keys for those who bowled (balls_bowled from the overs, maidens, runs_conceded, wickets, wides, no_balls), fielding keys from the dismissals (c = catches or wk_catches for the keeper, st = stumpings, run out = run_outs for the fielder named). The dismissal text per batter ("c Smith b Khan", "lbw b Patel", "retired") and the bowling figures as written ("4-0-23-2") go in a lore chunk on the event titled Scorecard, one line per batter and bowler, in the owner's words.
8. A Player of the Match: WON from the person to the event, title Player of the Match.
9. Season lines: update the team season line for both sides (played, won, lost, tied, drawn, no_results, points, runs_scored, balls_faced_total, runs_conceded, balls_bowled_total under the all-out and DLS rules, net_run_rate recomputed, as_of today, source derived) and each player's season line (sum the match line in, games_played plus one, as_of). Do this in the same reply as the match, never later.
10. Say what you logged in cricket words: "Logged: we won by 5 wickets with 8 balls to spare, Jordan 47 off 38, Priya 2 for 23. That's 6 wins from 9, NRR up to +0.41."
Reconciliation: when a batting total minus extras does not equal the sum of individual scores, or the bowlers' runs plus byes and leg byes do not equal the total, say which figure is off by how much and ask; store the owner's answer. Ten wickets means ten out_* across the card plus any absent batter noted in lore.
Photos of a scorebook: read the card out loud back to the owner in one block before saving, since handwriting and columns are easy to misread.

properties.trigger: the owner's own club side: who is available, picking the XI, the fixture list, match fees, teas, the club's averages, the league table they play in

data.short_description: The weekly rhythm of a club side the owner plays in or runs: availability without reasons, selection, the result, fees and teas as notes, the league table and end-of-season averages.

lore.title: The week
lore.content:
For the owner's own club side, the week has a shape. Each step is optional; follow the owner's lead.
Monday to Thursday, availability: the owner says who is in and who is out. Set availability on PLAYS_FOR (available, unavailable, doubtful, unknown) with no reason, ever: "working", "wedding", "crocked", "ill" are all unavailable. New names are a search first (variant spellings are rife in group chats), then a person with primary_role player, PLAYS_FOR with arrangement amateur, acquired_via signup, tag cricket and the club's tag. A friend's friend playing once is arrangement substitute, started and ended on the match date, per the base. Juniors playing up: is_minor true, first name and last initial, nothing else.
Thursday or Friday, selection: the owner names the XI (and a 12th). Create or confirm the match event (fixture list from the league usually exists as scheduled events; search before creating), PLAYED_IN for the XI with started true and lineup_order when the batting order is known, played false for the 12th. Check the eleven count and any House rules (registered players, division caps, overseas limits) and say if something looks off. Who is keeping wicket and who is captain on the day go on the edges.
Saturday, the result: rule/cricket_scorecard_entry. If all that arrives is "lost by 40, I got 12", log the result and the owner's own line and leave the rest for later; tag the event scorecard-pending so you can ask for the card next time.
After the match: match fees, teas and who is umpiring next week are lore on the event or the team (titles: Fees, Teas, Umpiring), never properties. Player of the Match or the club's own weekly award: WON to the event with the club's title for it (Champagne Moment, Golden Duck Club).
Standings: the league's published table, when the owner pastes it, goes on the team season lines with source official and as_of the date; your own computed table from the results is source derived, and when the two disagree you say so with both and ask which the owner trusts (leagues apply penalties and corrections that never reach the scorebook).
Season end: COMPETES_IN final_rank and outcome (promoted, relegated, champion, none), WON for the champion, averages for the club dinner (batting and bowling by the Stat keys formulas, with the qualification the club uses, e.g. minimum 5 innings or 50 overs, stated when you present them), then offer to open next season with the squad rolled over.
Tags owned by this app: saturday-xi, scorecard-pending, availability-week. Never put a person's whereabouts, work or health in the record, even as a note; "unavailable" is the whole fact.
